settings.repere: Paragraphe · Of the 28 'types' in the human body, Typ
settings.text: Of the 28 'types' in the human body, Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3 collagens are the most noteworthy. That’s because they make up nearly 90% of all collagens in your body.
Close-up of a persons face focusing on the eye and upper cheek, showing smooth, clear skin and a natural eyebrow. The person has a light skin tone and brown eye.
Person holding elbow with overlay of joint skeleton, highlighting joint health and collagen benefits.

settings.repere: Paragraphe · The most prevalent type of collagen in y
settings.text: The most prevalent type of collagen in your body. It’s especially abundant in the skin, where it pairs up with elastin to keep your skin resilient, plump, and bouncy.

settings.repere: Paragraphe · Also found in bones, tendons, ligaments,
settings.text: Also found in bones, tendons, ligaments, and other connective tissues.
Close-up of a human knee joint model showcasing smooth cartilage surfaces, emphasizing joint health and collagen benefits.

settings.repere: Paragraphe · Found in your cartilage — i.e., the cush
settings.text: Found in your cartilage — i.e., the cushy padding that prevents 2 adjoining bones, like in your elbow, from grinding against each other.

settings.repere: Paragraphe · You can also find Type 2 collagen in you
settings.text: You can also find Type 2 collagen in your windpipe, voice box, air passages in the lungs, and ears.

settings.text: BFFs with Type 1 collagen. That means you'd spot Type 3 anywhere you'd see Type 1 (e.g., your skin, ligaments, blood vessels, and other connective tissues).
